data.narrative:
SF Compute is a Series A-stage semiconductor company founded by Evan Conrad and Alex Gajewski that has raised $52M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a peer universe of 3 same-stage private companies in Chips & Semiconductors (SambaNova Systems at $11.0B, Rebellions at $2.3B, d-Matrix at $2.0B), alongside 3 public semiconductor comparables (ALAB, NVDA, AMD).

Two valuation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis, using total capital raised as a proxy for current value, applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A progression, yielding $104M. Peer-median analysis across the three same-sector, same-stage private companies produces $2.3B, with observed valuations ranging from $2.0B to $11.0B. Public-comp anchoring via price-to-sales (median 20.5x across semiconductor peers) cannot be applied due to the absence of disclosed revenue for SF Compute.

Triangulation of the two applicable methods supports a valuation range of $88M to $2.7B, with a median of $1.2B. The wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty regarding where SF Compute positions within its peer set—stage-progression suggests a conservative floor, while peer-median implies substantial upside if the company commands technology or market positioning closer to higher-valued peers. Key uncertainties include revenue trajectory, proprietary differentiation, and customer concentration.
